subject: Social Media
title: Privacy Is Dead
description: A 60-second lesson on Privacy Is Dead.

hook.text: Mark Zuckerberg said privacy is no longer a social norm. He said that while building a business on your data.

buildup.text: We share locations, photos, relationships, and health data daily. Most people don't know how much they reveal.

discovery.text: A 2019 study found the average person shares data with 350 companies per month without realizing it.

twist.text: People say they care about privacy but act otherwise. They share freely, skip terms, and ignore settings.

climax.text: This gap is the 'privacy paradox'—we value privacy in theory but trade it for convenience every single day.

punchline.text: Privacy isn't dead. We just keep selling it cheap.

quiz.question: What is the 'privacy paradox'?
options: People value privacy but trade it for convenience
Companies protect data but still get hacked
